rules.statement: Don't ask a private method to take a read-only collection interface such as `IReadOnlyList<T>` instead of `List<T>` when every caller passes a `List<T>`: CA1859 runs as an error and requires the concrete type there.
rules.why: The repositories build with the .NET analyzers as errors. CA1859 rejects an interface-typed parameter on a private method whose callers all pass the concrete type, so the indexer isn't called through an interface.
rules.check: Before reporting a concrete collection parameter, check whether the method is private or internal and whether every caller passes that concrete type. If so, CA1859 settles it, and the finding shouldn't be raised.

rules.statement: When a code comment or a design decision promises a behavior, such as service registrations of other kinds keeping their original position, add a test that exercises that case.
rules.why: If a later change broke the promised behavior, for example by moving or dropping those registrations, no test would fail, and hosts could silently change behavior.
rules.check: Look for comments or referenced decisions in changed production code that state a guarantee, especially about edge cases such as type- or factory-registered services. Confirm that a test in the diff or the test project covers it.
